## Headline

**NPS climbed to 52 (up from 48). Top-quartile for the industry segment**, CSAT held at 4.6/5, and median resolution time dropped 17.6% to 2.8 hours despite ticket volume rising 11.4%. At risk accounts cut nearly in half (20 → 14). The CX team absorbed an Enterprise onboarding wave without breaking quality.

## What moved

Q3 brought a **15-account NAMER Enterprise onboarding wave** that drove ticket volume from 5,240 → 5,840. a real workload spike. Despite that, **median resolution dropped from 3.4h to 2.8h**, a sustained 13-week downward trend that points to process gains, not headcount additions.

**NPS lifted 4 points to 52** across all segments, but the gain is Enterprise-led (NPS 64) with Mid Market following (51). **SMB lagged at 32**. Not declining, just stuck. **At risk accounts dropped from 20 to 14**, combined ARR exposure down to $2.4M. The proactive outreach playbook the team rolled out in W30 is showing up in the numbers.

## So what

The Q3 result demonstrates the **CX team can scale through ticket-volume growth without sacrificing quality**. a critical signal as we move into the up market motion that will drive ticket volume higher in Q4. The Enterprise NPS at 64 confirms the dedicated CSM model is working. Recommend extending dedicated coverage to top Mid Market accounts (currently they get pooled coverage). **At risk reduction is the highest-leverage finding**. $1.8M of ARR exposure cleared in 90 days through proactive outreach. Make this a standing program, not a Q3 initiative.

## Talking points

- **NPS 52 is top-quartile** for our industry segment. Worth leading the customer review with this
- **Enterprise NPS 64** confirms the dedicated CSM model is working. Mid Market at 51 is closing the gap (was 45 in Q1)
- **At risk accounts: 20 → 14**, $2.4M ARR exposure remaining. Cleared $1.8M of risk in 90 days through proactive outreach
- **Median resolution 2.8h** while volume grew 11.4%. The team is more efficient, not just bigger. Process gains (new playbook + escalation routing)
- **SMB NPS at 32** is the outlier. Not declining, but stuck. Worth a dedicated SMB retention experiment in Q4
- **78% of tickets close within 4 hours**. Strong distribution. The long tail (180 tickets > 24h) traces to feature requests, not bugs

## Risks + caveats

SMB NPS at 32 is the **structural concern**, not a Q3 problem. The combination of pooled coverage + lower spend creates an experience gap that NPS captures honestly. Recommend a dedicated SMB retention experiment in Q4. Even a lightweight "office hours" model could close the gap. The Mid Market NPS gain might also reflect a shift in MIX (we have onboarded more Mid Market accounts) rather than a per account experience lift. Worth segmenting in the next CX review. The Northwind Logistics P1 (TKT-26-09308) resolved in 48 minutes is the kind of incident that does not show in aggregates. Worth a postmortem since the customer was particularly visible.
